claims.text: The proposed predictive model incorporates descriptors of atomic-level disorder and vibrational properties.
Including atomic-disorder and vibrational descriptors will significantly improve identification of high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Configurational entropy and atomic size mismatch reflect the degree of atomic disorder in high-entropy alloys.
Greater atomic disorder enhances phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces thermal conductivity.
Quantitatively linking atomic-scale disorder and vibrational behavior to phonon scattering captures the interplay responsible for low thermal conductivity.
Capturing this interplay enables better discrimination of low-phonon-thermal-conductivity alloys than approaches using fewer or less relevant descriptors.
The proposed approach will produce a lower mean prediction error than current models.
The proposed approach will improve the ranking of candidate low-conductivity alloys relative to current models.
Current predictive or heuristic models rely on limited material descriptors.
Current predictive or heuristic models do not fully account for the interplay of atomic disorder and vibrational contributions.
The approach is expected to be applicable only to high-entropy alloys whose compositions and processing conditions fall within the characterized training regime.
Alloys with extreme or unconventional compositions or microstructures may not be accurately predicted.
The magnitude of prediction-error improvement depends on training-data quality and extent.
The magnitude of prediction-error improvement depends on descriptor selection.
